pull.title: validation: Ensure Invalid ValidationState has result
pull.body:
Block and transaction validation results are represented in `ValidationState`, and invalid results in "Invalid" states. Invalid validation results have a `result`, an enum value, and a `reject_reason`, a structured string.

The change is to ensure that an __invalid result always has a set result and reject reason__. This increases code robustness/security.

One instance was identified where the result was not set, and is being fixed by a new `BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE` result. PR #31981 moved a previous-block check from outside of `TestBlockValidity()` to inside it, and introduced a new usage of `BlockValidationState` with unset result. The result field is not checked outside. This instance is changed now to use the newly-introduced `BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE` value.

The new enum value is added to the kernel C API and its C++ wrapper. In P2P, a `BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE` result does not lead to punishing the peer.

A few test-only instances with empty reject reason are changed to use a dummy value ("dummy-reason").

History: this was found on the side of #35570, but left untouched there; see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35570#issuecomment-5739477357 and https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35570#discussion_r4075379069.

Alternatives considered:

1. Use a new reject reason enum. This is the cleanest solution, but the cost is the extension of a widely-used validation enum.
2. Use a different mechanism for returning this specific case from `TestBlockValidity()`, e.g. using `util::Expected`, as you discussed. No need to touch the `BlockValidationResult` enum. However, in the call sites of `TestBlockValidity()`, the reject reason and debug strings are handled similarly to other non-valid check results, and they would need a special handling.
3. Reuse an exisiting reject reason enum value in `TestBlockValidity()`, with the comment "only in this spot it means a little different thing".
4. Create a special `TestBlockValidationResult`, "on top of" `BlockValidationResult`, with the extra value, and a special `TestBlockValidationState` (`ValidationState<TestBlockValidationResult>`). Use this in `TestBlockValidity()`. As this is used only internally, within this methods and at its call sites, the new value+state doesn't have to be exposed. Therefore the change has lower impact.

crACK ba0d2b49f526b789ab758bc25f909344b2b092c1

Reviewed the invariant change and its blast radius:

- **Enum exhaustiveness / net handling:** `MaybePunishNodeForBlock`'s `switch` (net_processing.cpp:538) has no `default:`, so `BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE` had to be handled explicitly — the added `case ... break;` (no punishment) is right: the only producer is `TestBlockValidity()` (block-template/`submitblock` validity testing, not network-received blocks), so a peer should never be punished for it, and `break` keeps `nDoS` at 0. Matches @Sjors' point that the validity path doesn't consume the enum.
- **`reject_reason` now required + `Assume(!reject_reason.empty())`:** checked the callers that passed `""` — the fuzz targets `txdownloadman.cpp:223/357/420` and the `txdownload_tests.cpp` cases. These matter because `Assume` is **fatal under a fuzz build**, so an un-updated `Invalid(result, "")` would abort the fuzzer; the PR updates all of them to `"dummy-reason"`, so the invariant is complete.
- The real fix (`TestBlockValidity`: `Invalid({}, ...)` → `Invalid(BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE, ...)`) removes the one unset-result path.

Nit (non-blocking): the `BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE` comment — "...e.g. we don't have the block it's building on" — reads close to `BLOCK_MISSING_PREV` and doesn't match the actual use (`hashPrevBlock != tip`, "inconclusive-not-best-prevblk": builds on a *non-tip* block we may well have). Maybe "...the block it builds on is not the current tip" to disambiguate.

Code-review only (didn't build/run).

> Nit (non-blocking): the `BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE` comment ...

I acknowledge this, indeed the example could be closer to the current usage. I think it's very minor, as this is only an example in the comment. Not changing now (I don't want to invalidate existing acks), but will change if I need to touch for other reason.

> I acknowledge this, indeed the example could be closer to the current usage. I think it's very minor, as this is only an example in the comment.

I'd agree if this was a random test file, but comments in `consensus/validation.h` should be clear in my opinion - e.g. just from reading the file it wouldn't be clear which of the two enum values a block with a missing prev would get.

More generally, I find the state of the enum kind of confusing:
The preexisting `BLOCK_MISSING_PREV` , `BLOCK_HEADER_LOW_WORK` (and to some extent `BLOCK_TIME_FUTURE`)  all describe specific inconclusive scenarios (we don't know if it is valid, refuse to validate, or it may become valid in the future), so it's not clear to me what a `BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE` category should cover.  Is this meant to become a kitchen-sink category for "all the rest"?  Otherwise wouldn't it be more in line with the existing approach to call it `BLOCK_PREV_NOT_TIP` or similar?

Thinking about it more, I agree that reject reasons should be specific: a generic BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE is not much better than leaving the result unset, which is what this PR tries to eliminate. It's also exposed in the kernel API, so the name should be precise.

Given the background on how `TestBlockValidity()` is used, the options I see are:

- Add a new specific value, namely BLOCK_PREV_NOT_TIP (replacing BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE), with the auxiliary costs (e.g. exposing through kernel API).

- Don't add a new value, but reuse an existing one, e.g. BLOCK_MISSING_PREV, with a comment explaining the mismatch. Callers of `TestBlockValidity()` only look at the reject reason string, so the enum value isn't used there. (BLOCK_INVALID_PREV doesn't fit: it means the block is definitely invalid, and net_processing punishes peers for it.)

I lean towards the first option and will rename unless there are objections.

validation: Add BlockValidationResult::BLOCK_PREV_NOT_TIP

The goal is to ensure that an Invalid `ValidationState` always has a set result.
However, there is a violating usage in `TestBlockValidity`.
As a preparation, a new value is added to the `BlockValidationResult`
enum, `BLOCK_PREV_NOT_TIP`, representing a result for when
the block being mined is not built on top of the current tip.
In P2P, a `BLOCK_PREV_NOT_TIP` result does not lead to punishing the peer.
A corresponding value is added to the kernel C API
(btck_BlockValidationResult_PREV_NOT_TIP) and its C++ wrapper, though
not returned by current kernel API functions.
The new value is used in a later commit.

> Instead of expanding `BlockValidationResult` one could wrap the return value of `TestBlockValidity()` with `util::Expected` ...

That's also a potential solution, I agree. I categorize these approaches:

1. Use a new reject reason enum. This is the cleanest solution, but the cost is the extension of a widely-used validation enum.
2. Use a different mechanism for returning this specific case from `TestBlockValidity()`, e.g. using `util::Expected`, as you discussed. No need to touch the `BlockValidationResult` enum. However, in the call sites of `TestBlockValidity()`, the reject reason and debug strings are handled similarly to other non-valid check results, and they would need a special handling.
3. Reuse an exisiting reject reason enum value in `TestBlockValidity()`, with the comment "only in this spot it means a little different thing".

The latter two introduce inconsistencies in the code (a bit "hacky"), therefore I chose 1.
A more specific `BLOCK_PREV_NOT_TIP` sounds good to me.

The goal is to ensure that an Invalid `ValidationState` always has a set result.
A violating usage in `TestBlockValidity` is being changed: instead of the
default `BLOCK_RESULT_UNSET`, it now uses `BLOCK_PREV_NOT_TIP`.
The result field from `TestBlockValidity` is currently not inspected by callers,
but the constraint "an Invalid state must have a set result"
is satisfied this way.
Add a unit test to verify the reject reason in this case.

Changes applied:

- Renamed the new reject reason enum value to the more specific `BLOCK_PREV_NOT_TIP` (from `BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE`), as suggested by @mzumsande
- Added a unit test for the reject reason returned by `TestBlockValidity()`, as suggested by @hodlinator

(`git range-diff ba0d2b49f526b789ab758bc25f909344b2b092c1...be5ff46547675d6cd329aad7778a32f4192fe605`)

re-ACK be5ff46547675d6cd329aad7778a32f4192fe605

Switched to more precise enum name and added unit test.

I've came up with another solution alternative:

4. Create a special `TestBlockValidationResult`, "on top of" `BlockValidationResult`, with the extra value, and a special `TestBlockValidationState` (`ValidationState<TestBlockValidationResult>`). Use this in `TestBlockValidity()`. As this is used only internally, within this methods and at its call sites, the new value+state doesn't have to be exposed. Therefore the change has lower impact.

I've added this (and other alternatives) to the description.
I'm testing this solution, it seems better because it has less impact. Currently it can be seen here: https://github.com/optout21/bitcoin/pull/32

I'm looking forward for assessments from reviewers.

The change looks good from the tests I ran. miner_tests and txdownload_tests pass on the PR head, and reverting the validation.cpp change reproduces the failure in miner_tests.cpp:984 (BLOCK_PREV_NOT_TIP expected, but 0 returned). Restoring the change makes the test pass again as i saw , confirming the regression test covers the behavior introduced by this PR.

> I've came up with another solution alternative:
>> Create a special TestBlockValidationResult [...]

Adding a whole new `TestBlockValidationResult` enum just for one value seems overkill.

If I understand correctly:
- `BLOCK_PREV_NOT_TIP` means: it's not the tip, I didn't check the index
- `BLOCK_MISSING_PREV` means: it's not in the index (and therefore not the tip)

It's true that current p2p code doesn't use  `BLOCK_PREV_NOT_TIP`, and probably never needs it because it always looks through the headers. But it's still the _result of validation_.
